title: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning without Prompting
abstract: This paper explores the ability of large language models to reason without prompting, by altering the decoding process to uncover inherent chain-of-thought paths. The proposed CoT-decoding method reliably extracts these paths, leading to significant improvements in reasoning performance across various benchmarks.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a math problem, but instead of directly giving the answer, you break it down into smaller steps. This is similar to how large language models can reason without prompting, by uncovering inherent chain-of-thought paths.

We found that by altering the decoding process, we can reveal these paths, leading to improved reasoning performance.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
The CoT-decoding method works by considering alternative top-k tokens at the first decoding step, and then continuing with greedy decoding. This allows the model to explore different paths and uncover inherent chain-of-thought reasoning.

For example, in the GSM8K question, a valid CoT path emerges at k = 9, leading to the correct answer.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
We evaluated the CoT-decoding method on various benchmarks, including GSM8K, MultiArith, and Year Parity. The results show significant improvements in reasoning performance, with CoT-decoding achieving 72.0% accuracy on GSM8K and 95.0% accuracy on Year Parity.

These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the CoT-decoding method in uncovering inherent chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
The CoT-decoding method has significant implications for the development of large language models, as it allows for the evaluation of intrinsic reasoning capabilities without the need for human-provided prompts.

This can lead to more accurate assessments of model performance and a better understanding of the strengths and limitations of current models.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
The CoT-decoding method introduces several key innovations, including the use of alternative top-k tokens at the first decoding step, and the evaluation of answer confidence to select the most reliable decoding paths.

These innovations enable the CoT-decoding method to effectively uncover inherent chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models.
